clue.text: Prevent son taking what's best

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees
the top is the best of anything, as in 'top of the class'

explanation.surface: A son grabs the best of everything for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something before it happens is to block or prevent it.

clue.text: Very little poetry translated, that's surprising for Scots and Early English

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation of surprise or regret
EE is the abbreviation for Early English, the medieval architectural style

explanation.surface: A scrap of verse rendered into English startles readers in Scotland and medieval England.
explanation.walkthrough: A trochee is a single metrical foot (a stressed then an unstressed syllable), so it is a very small piece of poetry indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot is the smallest unit of verse, hence a tiny portion of poetry.

clue.text: He prepares material for internet ad in which Duke appears with accountant

indicators.note: in which ... appears places the duke and accountant inside the advertisement word

parts.note: a poster is an advertisement on a wall
CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An online advert features a duke alongside his accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who records audio shows for online download is preparing material for the internet.

clue.text: Struggling new governor's losing head (crucial moment)

indicators.note: struggling suggests things in disarray, so the letters of new and the beheaded governor are jumbled
losing head drops the first letter of the word governor

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A newly appointed governor is floundering and has lost his head at a critical juncture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' leaves OVERNOR; 'Struggling' rearranges NEW + OVERNOR into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A last chance that must be seized immediately is a decisive, critical point in time.

clue.text: Music that could worry trapeze performer?

definitions.meaning: a composition for nine players or voices
read as two words, the absence of a safety net below the trapeze, which would alarm an acrobat

explanation.definitionFit: A piece for nine instruments is a nonet, and split as NO NET it is the acrobat's fear of having nothing below to catch a fall.

clue.text: Cut short lively contest

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off the word

parts.note: warm can mean lively or heated, as in a warm debate

explanation.surface: A spirited competition is brought to an early end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' removes the final M from WARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations is a contest of force.

clue.text: Strong criticism of run before meal

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
a.p. is ante prandium, Latin for before a meal, used on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone is told off sharply for running off just before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: AP (ante prandium) is a pharmacist's Latin abbreviation many solvers will not know: it marks a dose taken before meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuke, as in a rap over the knuckles, is a sharp reprimand.

clue.text: Tree containing last of the island's resin

indicators.note: containing means the tree word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: an elm is a common deciduous tree

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word the

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A tree on an island yields a sticky resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts E (last of 'the') inside ELM to make ELEM, then the island's I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum exuded by tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: He interprets Bible texts (old), for example Peter's centrally featured

parts.note: ex- means former or old, as in ex-wife
eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: centrally featured takes the inner letters of the name, dropping its first and last

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Ancient scripture is studied, with St Peter's writings at the heart of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally featured' takes ETE, the middle of PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: An expounder of scripture explains its meaning, which is exactly what a biblical commentator does.

clue.text: Awkward retreat after court appearance?

indicators.note: after means the hideaway comes behind the wooing word

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a private retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles off clumsily after a stiff appearance before the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court appearance' suggests a trial, but court is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and clumsy movement or acting is described as lacking grace, like carved timber.

clue.text: It could make Peterlee almost full?

indicators.note: it could make signals that the letters can be rearranged into a new word
almost drops the final letter of the place name

explanation.surface: Could the County Durham town of Peterlee be nearly at capacity?
explanation.walkthrough: Peterlee is a town in County Durham, England. 'almost' cuts it to PETERLE, and 'It could make' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sated or filled to the brim is a synonym for full.

clue.text: Pressman's no small courage?

indicators.note: no means the letter is absent from the press baron's name

parts.note: William Randolph Hearst was the American newspaper magnate
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Is the newspaper man lacking in bravery?
explanation.walkthrough: Hearst was the American press baron; 'no small' removes S from HEARST.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage is sometimes called having heart, as in 'take heart' or 'lose heart'.

clue.text: Like some heating oldie's prepared collecting wood

indicators.note: collecting means the rearranged letters gather the timber word inside them
prepared suggests the word oldie is worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: A pensioner gets ready by gathering firewood for the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oldie's' reads as 'oldie is', so 'prepared' is the anagram signal; the wood goes into the middle of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A central heating system burning fuel oil in a boiler is described this way.

clue.text: Girl drinks fashionable mineral

indicators.note: drinks means the girl's name swallows the other word

parts.note: Olive is a girl's name
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A young woman sips a trendy mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate rock-forming mineral, the gem form being peridot.

clue.text: Store and accumulate? Yes, in fortified position that's unfinished …

indicators.note: in places the word for yes inside the shortened defensive line
that's unfinished drops the final letter of the word for the fortification

parts.note: a line is a fortified military position, as in the Maginot Line
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A garrison is told to gather supplies and stockpile them in a half-built fort.
explanation.walkthrough: A defensive line is a fortified position in military language (the Maginot Line); the trailing dots lead into 15 down, which points back to this fort.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock up for later use, as with provisions for winter, is to build up a supply.

clue.text: Truly anti-English in conflict? Not this State

indicators.note: in conflict suggests the letters fighting each other into disorder

explanation.surface: A truly anti-English nation at war would not be staying out of the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S tempts you to look for a country, but State means a condition: the one you are not in when in conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to take sides in a war is the condition opposite to being at war.

clue.text: here, perhaps, in style of the moment?

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
mo is short for moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: The fort mentioned before may be found here, dressed in the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 13 down's fortified position: 'here, perhaps' points to that fort, the Texas mission besieged in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo, a mission in San Antonio, Texas, was a famous fortified position in the Texan war of independence.

clue.text: Part of Far East?

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie inside the words Far East

explanation.surface: A piece of the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or region is a portion of a larger territory such as the Orient.

clue.text: High flier cruelly taunts a couple of rookies

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the letters are knocked about into a different order
a couple of means the first two letters of the word rookies

explanation.surface: A space traveller mercilessly mocks a pair of new recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of rookies' gives RO; 'cruelly' rearranges TAUNTS + A + RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller flies higher than anyone, quite literally.

clue.text: Russian's attempt to stop Irish?

indicators.note: to stop means plugging the gap inside the abbreviation for Irish

parts.note: a go is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: A Russian tries to block an Irish opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is a typical man's name in Russia, so a Russian person in crossword terms.

clue.text: With specialised knowledge, getting no stick when downsizing

indicators.note: when downsizing says the phrase is cut down to a smaller run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: An expert escapes all criticism while making staff redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the last of 'getting' through 'no' to most of 'stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnostic means having esoteric spiritual insight, from the Greek for knowing.

clue.text: Turning away a loan tie-in? Unexpected

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters come out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A bank loan linked to another deal turns customers off, surprisingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement, the act of pushing someone away or making them hostile, is a turning away.

clue.text: Greatly offend university tutor heartlessly-over long period

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, means the earlier letters sit above the period word

parts.note: OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle letters of the word tutor, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A heartless university tutor causes great offence over a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is the UK's distance-learning university. In a down entry 'over' means placed above, so the long period sits at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrage someone is to shock and anger them deeply.

clue.text: Solitary individuals seen in African port

indicators.note: seen in places the individuals word within the port's name

parts.note: Lome is the capital and main port of Togo
ones are single individuals

explanation.surface: Lone figures are spotted in a West African harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lonely and on one's own is the sense of solitary.

clue.text: In Spain and Italy nun strangely gets listless feeling

indicators.note: In at the front places the scrambled nun between the two country letters

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (Espana)
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of nun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun in Spain and Italy oddly suffers from boredom.
explanation.walkthrough: E and I are international vehicle codes, the convention setters use for countries; 'In' at the front wraps them round the jumbled nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weariness and boredom, a lack of energy or interest.

clue.text: Turn to buy Guinness maybe when time's hard?

indicators.note: when ... 's says the time letter is replaced by the hard letter

parts.note: Guinness is the best-known Irish stout
T is the abbreviation for time
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is your round to buy the Guinness when times are tough.
explanation.walkthrough: A shout is British and Australian slang for one's turn to buy a round of drinks, as in 'my shout'.
explanation.definitionFit: In pub slang one's round of drinks is called a shout.

clue.text: Girl that's supporting Texas, maybe?

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, means the that-is letters sit beneath the others

parts.note: Texas is an example of somewhere in the Southern US
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A woman cheers on the Lone Star State.
explanation.walkthrough: S for Southern plus US: Texas is a state in the southern US.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a girl's name, a pet form of Susan.

clue.text: Operating in cramped surroundings later in the day

indicators.note: in places the operating word inside the cramped word

parts.note: tight means cramped, here the enclosing word
on means operating, as in 'the machine is on'

explanation.surface: Surgery is carried out in a confined space this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is the part of the current day still to come.

clue.text: Soldier's new drink

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier tries a new beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a juniper-flavoured spirit, a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Instrument's lacking a container

indicators.note: lacking means the instrument's name is without the letter a

parts.note: a tuba is a large brass instrument

explanation.surface: The brass instrument is missing its case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking a' removes A from TUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a round open vessel for holding things.

clue.text: Rating England keeper

definitions.meaning: a rating is a naval sailor without officer rank
David ... was England's football goalkeeper in the 1990s

explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary sailor is a naval rating, and David Seaman kept goal for England's football team.

clue.text: A badly-drafted lab notice as such could put you in the dock?

definitions.text: could put you in the dock?

indicators.note: badly-drafted suggests the words lab and notice are put together wrongly, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A carelessly written laboratory sign might land its author in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The dock is where the accused stands in a British court; the A stays at the front while 'badly-drafted' scrambles only the lab notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct giving grounds for a lawsuit could lead to someone standing trial.

clue.text: Young one needs space after first date ends

indicators.note: after means the printing space comes behind the final letters
ends picks the last letter of each of the words first and date; the run of letters across date ends is a coincidence, not a hidden word

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A youngster needs some room once a first date is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives T and E, the last letters of 'first' and 'date'; 'after' puts EN behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person.
